newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-GRITSCHUK AND PLATOV WIN DANCE GOLD.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-GRITSCHUK AND PLATOV WIN DANCE GOLD.

text.p: Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov produced a spectacular interpretation of Arab culture and gained a second set of perfect 6.0 scores to retain their European ice dance title on Friday.

It was the third victory of the week for Russia as they edged towards an unprecedented sweep of the titles, which they will achieve if holder Irina Slutskaya hangs on to her lead to win the women's gold on Saturday afternoon.
Alexei Urmanov won the men's title and Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov the pairs earlier in the week.

But Friday's triumph turned slightly sour when the couple's former coach, Natalia Linichuk, whose camp in Delaware Gritschuk and Platov left just over a month ago to join Tatiana Tarasova in Moscow, claimed credit for devising the programme.
Gritschuk denied this was true. "Honestly, we did this ourselves. Natalia was hardly helping us at all in Deleware. We did our own choreography.
"We had one meeting for one hour with an Arab man in New York to learn the moves. But the choreography was our own. No one helped us with this."
The Olympic and world champions turned to the Middle East for inspiration and their evocative creation brought another set of maximum scores from the nine-judge panel.
Their 6.0s for artistry gave them 12 for the competition. They received six on Thursday for the presentation of their original dance, the Tango.
Their superb programme was performed to music by the Peter Gabriel, former lead singer of the pop group Genesis.
"It was our most difficult programme. But we decided last season we wanted to do this. And Tatiana has added a lot to it in just one month," Platov said.
Fellow Russians Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov skated a highly dramatic and passionate waltz to "Masquerade" by Russian composer Khatchaturian and gained a highly deserved second place.
On another night against lesser rivals, it would have been worth victory.
They had seven 5.9s for artistry and won the vote of one of the judges against their rivals.
"It is a start," the dark-haired Krylova said. "We worked so hard and for such a long time on this.
"It is different from anything we have ever done but we wanted to do something different to show people that we can skate everything."
French couple Sophie Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy held on to take third place from team mates Marina Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat, who also skated an Arab number.
The bronze medallists were delighted after missing 18 months of skating because Moniotte sustained an ankle injury in 1995.
"Taking into account what we have been through, this is wonderful," said Moniotte.
